notes.meaning: A written family record begins here, tracing Adam's family line down to Noah. It looks back to the day God created human beings in his own likeness. God made people to reflect his goodness and to enjoy fellowship with him.

God created humanity as male and female, poured out his blessing on them, and gave them the shared name "man" or mankind. Giving them one name points to the close and lasting union between a husband and wife.

When Adam reached 130 years of age, he fathered a son named Seth who was born in Adam's own likeness and image. While Adam was originally created pure in God's image, Seth inherited his father's fallen and mortal condition. Yet God preserved a seed through Seth to keep true worship alive.

Adam lived 800 more years after Seth was born and fathered many other sons and daughters. During this long lifespan, Adam was able to teach many generations about the creation, the fall, and God's promise of mercy.

Adam lived for 930 years before he died, fulfilling the sentence God gave in the garden of Eden. Even though early humans enjoyed remarkably long lives, physical death still came to the father of the human race.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars compare these great lifespans to ancient Mesopotamian king lists, suggesting the large numbers were symbolic ways of honoring revered ancient ancestors.

notes.meaning: Seth was 105 years old when he became the father of Enosh. This family line carried forward the worship of the true God and led directly toward the coming Savior.

differ.view: The phrase "became the father of" indicates a direct father-to-son link with no missing names, providing an unbroken timeline.
Biblical genealogies often skip generations to focus on key figures, so these names establish legal family lineage rather than a strict calendar.

notes.meaning: After Enosh was born, Seth lived 807 years and had other sons and daughters. God blessed his household with many children to help fill the earth.
Seth lived a total of 912 years, and then he died. Like his father Adam, he reached an advanced age, but he still could not escape bodily death.
Enosh reached 90 years of age and became the father of Kenan. Scripture notes this son specifically because he continued the godly line of faith.
Enosh lived 815 years after Kenan was born and had more sons and daughters. His family continued to expand over many centuries.
Enosh lived 905 years in all, and then he died. The steady refrain "and he died" reminds the reader that death reigned over all of Adam's descendants.
When Kenan was 70 years old, he became the father of Mahalalel. God kept preserving the promised line through each succeeding generation.
Kenan lived 840 years after Mahalalel was born and had other sons and daughters. He provided leadership and guidance for his growing clan.
Kenan lived a total of 910 years, and then he died. Even the most respected leaders among the patriarchs had to face the grave.
Mahalalel was 65 years old when he became the father of Jared. God continued to guide the family chain that would eventually lead to Noah.
Mahalalel lived 830 years after Jared was born and fathered other sons and daughters. His days were filled with family life and the care of his home.
Mahalalel lived 895 years, and then he died. Sin's curse continued to bring every earthly life to an inevitable close.
Jared lived 162 years and became the father of Enoch. This birth brought into the world a man who would stand out for his rare holiness.
After Enoch was born, Jared lived another 800 years and had more sons and daughters. He saw the world change and grow around him through eight centuries.
Jared lived a total of 962 years, making him the second-oldest man recorded in Scripture, and then he died. His enormous lifespan still came to a full stop.
When Enoch was 65 years old, he became the father of Methuselah. Becoming a father seems to have marked the start of an even deeper dedication to God.

Enoch walked with God for 300 years after Methuselah was born, while raising a family. Walking with God means living in close, constant fellowship with him, seeking his pleasure and trusting his will in everyday life.

differ.view: Enoch's steady walk shows that believers can, through God's sanctifying grace, live without committing sin.
Enoch walked in true faith and communion with God, but believers remain imperfect and continue to battle sin throughout this life.

notes.meaning: Enoch lived a total of 365 years on earth. His years were far fewer than those of the other patriarchs, yet his life was full and deeply pleasing to the Lord.

Enoch walked closely with God, and then he disappeared because God took him directly to heaven without letting him die. This miracle showed that death is not the end of human existence and rewarded Enoch's faithful devotion.

other.label: Orthodox
other.view: Many early church fathers taught that Enoch was preserved alive in his physical body and will return with Elijah to serve as one of the two prophetic witnesses before the end of the world.

notes.meaning: Methuselah was 187 years old when he became the father of Lamech. His name pointed forward to a sending forth, giving an early sign of coming judgment.
After Lamech was born, Methuselah lived 782 years and had other sons and daughters. God spared him through many centuries as a sign of his great patience with an ungodly world.

Methuselah lived for 969 years, the longest life recorded in the Bible, and then he died. The numbers show he died in the very year the flood came, showing that even the longest earthly life must at last reach an end.
When Lamech was 182 years old, he had a son. This Lamech was from Seth's godly line, unlike the violent man of the same name descended from Cain.

Lamech named his son Noah, which sounds like words meaning rest and comfort, hoping this son would bring relief from the painful toil caused by God's curse on the soil. Spoken by faith, this name pointed forward to the comfort God would bring through Noah.
After Noah was born, Lamech lived 595 years and had other sons and daughters. He spent these years working the ground alongside his family.
Lamech lived a total of 777 years, and then he died. He passed away shortly before the flood arrived, spared from witnessing the destruction of the world.

When Noah was 500 years old, he became the father of Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Shem is named first because the covenant promise and the lineage of the Messiah would flow through his family, even though Japheth was likely the eldest son.
